title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) to the most vulnerable drought-affected households in Burhakaba

description.narrative: ltpgtPASOS is proposing immediate lifesaving project by provision of unconditional cash transfers UCT to communities affected by the severe drought in the following 10 project locations: Araay, Awyaayi, Balow, Iboti, Aw-ooyow, Burhakaba Wadaag, Burhakaba Waberi, Burhakaba Wadajir, Mususow and Aw Uurwayne villages, Burhakaba District of Bay region Somalia. The proposed intervention is guided by the findings of IPC Somalia Food Security outlook September 2025. The food insecurity situation in Somalia is worsening with 3.4 million people experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above) across Somalia. Between July and September 2025, around 624,000 people (3 percent of the population) have been experiencing Emergency levels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 4), while more than 2.8 million people (15 percent of the population) have been experiencing IPC Phase 3 (Crisis). lt/pgtltpgtNeeds assessment conducted by PASOS in Buurhakaba in October 2025 identified food, water, and protection as priority needs in the target settlements. The proposed activity will also address the negative coping mechanisms that affected populations have adopted as a result of the current measures' inadequacy of food, water, and lack of protection mechanisms. It will also prevent further displacement in Somalia as the affected people will be assisted in their locations in Buurhakaba.ltbrgtCash assistance is seen as the most suitable assistance as markets in Buurhakaba are operational and accessible with the essential food commodities available for purchase.ltbrgtIn this response, 1905 households - approximately 11430 persons (3150 women, 2905 men, 2632 boys and 2740 girls) in Buurhakaba are proposed to receive assistance. The intervention will target people in IPC phase 3+ with priority for households with individuals who have disability and female headed households.ltbrgtPASOS seeks to provide 55 USD per household for every round. This is in line with the Somalia Cash working Group and Food Security Cluster guideline for the transfer value for the Somalia Minimum expenditure basket (MEB). Each of the target household will receive 55 USD for 3 rounds in the months of February, March and April 2026. This will cover significant part of the MEB ( 70% ).ltbrgtThe assistance is critical in the context of the huge funding cuts for humanitarian operations in Somalia. PASOS will employ vulnerability-based targeting where prioritization will be applied to ensure the resources go those who are most vulnerable.ltbrgtFor transparent implementation, all registration will be done by PASOS monitoring and evaluation team together with the project staff. All beneficiaries will be issued with a SIM card so that is easier for them to be registered and get their entitlements with through mobile money transfer. ltbrgtPASOS values coordination of humanitarian response. It is this spirit that while implementing this project, all activities will be implemented in coordination with the Food Security cluster partners to ensure there is no duplication of assistance. PASOS will also coordinate with other SHF partners in the areas to ensure there is complementarity, and the targeted people get the maximum benefit of the project.ltbrgtlt/pgt
